points.description: Initialisation: arranges the neurons/weights in a lattice (topology) and initialises the weights randomly (different small values).

levels.says: Mentions only one of topology arrangement or random initialisation.

points.description: Sampling and similarity matching: samples an input vector from the input space and finds the winning neuron (best matching unit, e.g. minimum distance to the input).

levels.says: Mentions only sampling or only winner selection.

points.description: Update: updates the weights of the winning neuron and its neighbours according to the neighbourhood function (and learning rate), moving them toward the input.

Iteration and termination: shrinks the neighbourhood radius and decays the learning rate each iteration, and repeats from sampling until ordering/convergence is reached (or the iteration limit), then stops.

levels.says: Mentions only the loop/stopping condition or only the decay of radius/learning rate.

rubric.notes: Full marks need all four stages of SOM learning in a pseudo-code-like ordered form: initialise, sample and match, update winner and neighbours, decay and loop until convergence. Award half of a point if only part of it is given. Do not award marks for unrelated algorithms such as backpropagation.
